text.headline: Silver Slumps Amid Pressure Across Industrial Metals
text.tone: Precious and industrial contracts retreated sharply as investors weighed the drag of non-yielding assets alongside shifting currency movements.
lead: Silver led a broad retreat across hard assets, sliding 4.4% to $46.94 in a session marked by heavy commodity selling. The drop outpaced softer declines elsewhere in the sector and extended its monthly loss to 16.5%. While broader risk sentiment remained subdued, the scale of the move highlighted acute vulnerability in dual-purpose metals relative to purely defensive assets.

Industrial exposure appears to explain the depth of the decline, as detailed on the [[metals|Hard Assets Terminal]]. More than half of silver demand comes from industry, meaning it trades partly like a factory metal. It fell in tandem with platinum, which dropped 2.9% to $1,447, and copper, reflecting softer expectations for global industrial and automotive manufacturing demand.

Macroeconomic factors reinforced the move, as non-yielding commodities faced persistent competition from fixed-income yields. In the latest data, the benchmark US 10-year yield stood at 5.15%, raising the opportunity cost of holding metals that generate no income. A firmer dollar accompanied this interest-rate backdrop, pushing the euro down 0.3% against the greenback on the [[crypto|Crypto & Currencies]] page.

Looking ahead, market participants will track whether industrial demand signals stabilize or if further declines in factory metals like copper materialize. The trajectory of sovereign bond yields remains critical, as any renewed push higher would challenge non-yielding assets. Investors should review the [[outlook|Market Outlook]] to gauge how broad macro regimes navigate these evolving pressures.

briefs.markets: In the latest data, the 10-year yield reached 5.15% while large-cap equities slipped 0.6%, tracked on [[markets|Financial Markets]].
briefs.energy: In the latest data, natural gas rose 3.8% to $3.00, detailed on the [[energy|Energy Terminal]].
briefs.crypto: Bitcoin fell 0.6% to $64,941 as the euro weakened 0.3% against the dollar on [[crypto|Crypto & Currencies]].
briefs.metals: Silver fell 4.4% to $46.94 and platinum lost 2.9% on the [[metals|Hard Assets Terminal]].
briefs.estate: Global housing markets show divergence, with Moldova up 33.7% while China slid 6.3% on the [[estate|Estate Index]].
briefs.corporate: Credit conditions remained calm under a risk-on regime, tracked on the [[corporate|Corporate Monitor]].
briefs.outlook: The quarterly regime is risk-off as equity benchmarks sit below key moving averages, per the [[outlook|Market Outlook]].
briefs.islamic: The shariah benchmark fell 0.7% to 116.90 in the latest data on the [[islamic|Islamic Investment]] page.

watch: Crypto regulation news volume rose to 1.68x normal, though digital token prices have not yet reacted directly to fund flow developments.
Industrial metal pricing to see if persistent weakness in copper and platinum continues to drag dual-purpose assets like silver lower.
